_comment: Predeclared detection control for #26, committed before it runs. The first live selection run (2026-09-27, https://github.com/cooneycw/skillc/issues/26#issuecomment-5856746724) observed no skill invocation in any arm; this control asks whether that zero could have been anything else. It is protocol section 2's 'Detection control', kept distinct from the benefit comparison (ADR 0002), and it is NOT a selection result: the prompt names the skill.

arms.treatment: the collection installed (as in the selection run) and the canary instruction names 'qa-test'
arms.baseline: nothing installed, the same named instruction - the skill cannot be read because it is not there

expected.treatment: selected - the transcript shows the agent reading .../skills/qa-test/SKILL.md, detected by the codex heuristic
expected.baseline: anything except selected - with no skill installed the named canary cannot be satisfied, so an unknown/inconclusive result is the expected shape, not a failure

proves: the installed collection, the codex client, the transcript adapter and the recorded skill_invocations can report a real invocation of an installed skill in this exact configuration, and do not report one where none could happen
does_not_prove: that an UNPROMPTED selection would be detected when it happens by a different route (a relative path, another reader tool), or any sensitivity to a subtle description change - that is the degraded-description variant suggested on #26 (2026-09-26), not run here
failure_means: if the treatment arm does not read selected, the first run's zeros are not evidence of non-selection and must be reported as a detector gap
